title: scion-hub chart values
description: Values understood by the scion-hub chart. Unknown keys are rejected rather than ignored, so a misspelled key is an error and not a silent no-op.

global.description: Reserved by Helm for umbrella charts and unused by this chart. It must be declared: Helm merges an umbrella chart's .Values.global into every subchart and then validates the merged values against the subchart's own schema, so without this property any parent that sets any global key makes this chart impossible to depend on, with an error naming global rather than anything the operator wrote.

acknowledgeHAUnlanded.description: Acknowledge that these values describe an HA deployment this release cannot start. database.driver=postgres, or storage.provider=gcs with auth.mode=proxy, or hub.extraEnv setting K_SERVICE, each satisfy the hub's isHADeployment test (cmd/server_foreground.go:927); the hosted HA preflight then runs and several of its thirteen gates have no source in this chart (which ones is derived, not asserted here: see deploy/helm/scion-hub/hack/ha-gates.txt), so the hub aborts at cmd/server_foreground.go:151-153 before serving. Temporary key: it is removed when the Cloud SQL and ingress/IAP values have both landed.

replicaCount.description: More than one replica breaks the web terminal, exec, log tailing and port forwarding for roughly (N-1)/N of requests.

type.description: Empty resolves to Recreate at one replica and RollingUpdate above it. That default is a preference and not a safety measure: every value is accepted at every replica count. It is not free of data consequences, though: with no server.database.url the hub defaults its SQLite file to /home/scion/.scion/hub.db (pkg/config/hub_config.go:691), which lands in the scion-home emptyDir this chart mounts, so RollingUpdate's two-pod window has each pod writing its own copy and the loser's writes are discarded. Recreate cannot produce that overlap. Nothing is shared, so nothing is corrupted - writes are lost, bounded by the rollout window. When the Cloud SQL and Filestore values add shared state, concurrent instances are coordinated by the hub's Postgres advisory locks rather than by this field. At one replica the trade is an outage that loses PTY sessions and port tunnels (Recreate) against a window with two pods in which the web terminal and exec reach the wrong one about half the time (RollingUpdate, which renders maxUnavailable: 0).

repository.description: REQUIRED, with no default. A hub image built from the root Dockerfile with --target hub-gke - a stage the accompanying image-build change adds and which is not in the root Dockerfile yet. It is not published anywhere, so any default the chart could ship would point at an empty path or at another artifact. The published artifact named scion-hub is not this image: it runs as root, and it is built with -tags no_embed_web so it has no embedded web UI.

tag.description: Defaults to the chart appVersion. Mutually exclusive with digest.

digest.description: Preferred over tag. Mutually exclusive with it.

items.description: Each entry is {name: <secret>}. Typed strictly because a misspelling here validates as a bare object and then silently pulls nothing.

name.description: Display name for the hub. Cosmetic.

baseUrl.description: REQUIRED, with no default. External URL the hub is reached at. Must be https://: the session cookie's Secure attribute is derived from this prefix, so an http:// value serves session cookies without Secure. Omitting it is not an error in the hub - it warns and falls back to http://localhost, which agents cannot reach - so the chart requires it.

home.description: The hub's home directory. settings.yaml, storage/, templates/ and scion-token all live in <home>/.scion, and this is the only lever on that path: there is no SCION_HOME and no config-path flag. Must be writable by the container's uid.

adminMode.description: Truthy values are true, 1 and yes. Empty leaves the variable unset.

extraEnv.description: Extra container environment variables as Kubernetes EnvVar objects. Whether a SCION_SERVER_* name binds depends on a lookup table (camelCaseFields, pkg/config/hub_config.go:919): SCION_SERVER_DATABASE_URL binds, SCION_SERVER_DATABASE_MAX_OPEN_CONNS is discarded with no error, and nothing in the name says which. SCION_SERVER_DATABASE_* and SCION_SERVER_OIDC_* are rejected by the render because both outcomes are wrong here - a name that binds is applied after settings.yaml and wins, so the hub runs a configuration this chart never rendered and its guards never saw, and a name that is discarded is still reported to the admin server-config view as an active override. Configure those through config.extra.

hubId.description: REQUIRED, with no default. The hub's stable identity, supplied explicitly by the operator and used verbatim. The chart never generates or derives it: with no explicit value the hub derives its ID from its hostname, which on a Deployment is random per pod, so replicas silently diverge onto different blob-storage prefixes and secret scopes. Must be identical across upgrades. The empty string and leading or trailing whitespace are rejected.

args.description: Extra arguments APPENDED to the hub command. Appended is literal and it is the hazard: pflag is last-wins, so a flag the chart already renders would be silently replaced rather than rejected by the hub. Nothing at runtime prevents that - what prevents it is a reserved list checked at render time in scion-hub.hubArgs, which refuses the chart's own flags, flags that change which configuration the hub selects, flags that are not the lever they appear to be, flags whose value a later phase delivers through another channel, and flags that weaken authentication. An argument naming or carrying secret material also fails the render.

securityContext.description: runAsNonRoot is deliberately not a property here. The chart always sets it true, on both the pod and the hub container, and additionalProperties is false so it cannot be reintroduced as an override. Zero is rejected for runAsUser and runAsGroup because it contradicts that.

podAnnotations.description: Free-form annotations on the hub pod. scion.io/hub-id is rejected: it is rendered from hub.hubId and a second source for the hub's identity is the divergence the explicit hub ID exists to prevent.

podLabels.description: Free-form labels on the hub pod, for organisations that mandate cost-allocation or network-policy labels. Selector labels are rejected: a Deployment's selector is immutable after creation, so overriding one produces a Deployment that either fails to update or adopts no pods. Values must be strings; a bare number here is not a valid label value to Kubernetes.

probes.description: Probe paths are not configurable. Every HTTP probe targets the literal /readyz.

enabled.description: Turning the startup probe off is only permitted while probes.liveness.enabled is false; the template refuses the other combination. See probes.startup.failureThreshold.

periodSeconds.description: One of the two factors in the startup budget. This bound only keeps it positive; see probes.startup.failureThreshold for the bound that matters.

failureThreshold.description: The startup budget is periodSeconds x failureThreshold, and it must be at least 300s because first boot runs an ordered sequence of schema and data migration steps before the listener binds, so a pod killed part-way through leaves a partially applied migration. The 300 is a margin sized for a first boot against Cloud SQL behind the schema-migration advisory lock, which a later phase adds; it is not a measured SQLite figure. THIS SCHEMA DOES NOT ENFORCE THAT: a per-field minimum cannot express a product, so JSON Schema can only keep each factor positive. The 300s minimum is enforced at render time in scion-hub.assertStartupBudget, which is where to look and where to change it.

timeoutSeconds.description: Must exceed 2 seconds: the readiness handler's workspace mount check has its own 2 second internal timeout, and the kubelet default of 1 second would cut it off before the hub could report the failure.

liveness.description: Disabled by default, and always a TCP check on the web port when enabled: /readyz folds in external dependencies, so a liveness probe on it would kill healthy pods during a database failover.

service.description: The Service is always ClusterIP: the ingress path this chart targets is container-native load balancing through a network endpoint group, which requires it.

gcpServiceAccount.description: Workload Identity target. Must be a fully qualified Google service account address.

agentNamespace.description: Optional alias for runtime.namespace. If both are set they must agree.

namespace.description: Namespace agent pods are created in. Defaults to the release namespace.

imageRegistry.description: Registry prefix agent images are pulled from. Rendered as the top-level image_registry key of settings.yaml.

config.description: The hub's own configuration, delivered as a rendered settings.yaml rather than as environment variables: whether a SCION_SERVER_* name binds is decided by a lookup table (camelCaseFields, pkg/config/hub_config.go:919), the ones that miss it are discarded with no error, and the ones that hit it override the rendered file and win.

existingSecret.description: Name of a Secret with a settings.yaml key, used instead of the chart's rendered one. Mutually exclusive with config.extra, storage.bucket and agents.imageRegistry; supplying both fails the render. Nothing validates the contents of a Secret you bring yourself.

extra.description: Additional settings.yaml content, deep-merged over the rendered document. The chart's invariants are re-checked on the merged result, so an override that disables hosted mode or contradicts the rendered database driver fails the render.

database.description: Rendered into settings.yaml in full. Setting these through the environment instead is refused: driver and url do bind as SCION_SERVER_DATABASE_DRIVER and SCION_SERVER_DATABASE_URL, are applied after the rendered file and win, and would leave the chart's HA guards reasoning about a driver the hub is not using; maxOpenConns does not bind at all, because its koanf tag contains an underscore.

name.description: MINLENGTH, NOT MERELY REQUIRED. values.yaml ships name as the empty string, so the key is always present and "required" alone is satisfied by it - the check would pass on exactly the input it exists to reject. The same applies to user and password below.

then.description: REQUIRED WITH NO DEFAULT, and only where it is consequential. database.auth selects between IAM and password authentication, and neither is the default: the design made the default contingent on a live IAM verification against Cloud SQL, that verification has not been run (no cluster; 403 on the service account, recorded in VALIDATION.md), and an unverified default renders identically to a verified one. Requiring it only under postgres is deliberate - sqlite has no authentication mode, so forcing a choice there would be a meaningless choice, and a meaningless required key trains operators to set required keys without reading them.

Under password auth both the role and the password must be supplied. Under iam they must not be needed: the role is derived from the Google service account and there is no password at all, which is the entire point of that mode.

password.description: REFUSED under iam rather than ignored. A password set alongside iam means the operator believes one of the two is in effect and cannot tell which; silently dropping it would leave them believing the database is password-protected when the DSN carries no password at all.

driver.description: sqlite is single-pod only: it is a file in the hub's home directory. postgres turns on the hub's HA preflight, which additionally requires the hub ID, a database URL, GCS storage with a bucket and a durable session secret.

auth.description: REQUIRED under driver postgres, with NO DEFAULT. iam authenticates as the pod's Google service account and the DSN carries no password; password renders a Postgres role and password into the settings Secret. The absence of a default is the decision, not an oversight: the IAM path is unverified rather than known-good, defaulting to password when IAM would have worked is a silent security regression nothing would surface, and a withheld default can be added later without breaking any install while a wrong default cannot be removed without breaking every install.

name.description: The Postgres database name. Required under driver postgres.

user.description: The Postgres role. Under auth iam, leave empty to derive it from serviceAccount.gcpServiceAccount by stripping the trailing .gserviceaccount.com, which is the truncated form Cloud SQL registers IAM principals under. Setting it explicitly under iam is allowed and is checked against that derivation.

password.description: Only under auth password, and only ever inside the settings Secret - it is interpolated into server.database.url in the rendered settings.yaml and reaches no ConfigMap, annotation or argv. Use config.existingSecret to keep it out of Helm values entirely.

maxOpenConns.description: Keep above the number of background workers, and keep the total across replicas below the database tier's connection limit.

cloudsql.description: The Cloud SQL Auth Proxy. cloudsqlconn is not in the hub's go.mod, so the in-process connector is unavailable and the proxy is the only route to Cloud SQL.

instanceConnectionName.description: project:region:instance. Required when enabled. The pattern checks the three-part shape rather than merely that the string is non-empty: the proxy's own failure on a malformed value is a connection timeout, which reads as a network problem and sends the operator to the VPC rather than to this value.

nativeSidecar.description: An initContainers entry with restartPolicy: Always, started before the main container and torn down after it (GKE 1.29+). Set false only below 1.29, where the proxy becomes a plain sidecar with no ordering guarantee and the hub crash-loops until it wins the race - NOTES.txt prints that warning.

privateIp.description: Connect to the instance's private IP. Requires a VPC-native cluster peered to the instance.

port.description: The loopback port the proxy listens on. It is interpolated into the derived DSN, so the two cannot drift.

healthCheckPort.description: The proxy's own health-check server, serving /startup, /readiness and /liveness. Distinct from the hub's /readyz. Every container in the pod shares one network namespace, so this must not collide with hub.webPort - the chart refuses the collision rather than letting one process fail to bind at runtime.

digest.description: REQUIRED. The proxy is pinned by digest and there is no tag-only path: a tag can be repointed underneath a running cluster, and this container holds the credentials to the database.

storage.description: The hub's blob store. Not the workspace share agent pods mount, which is a separate subsystem.

provider.description: local keeps blobs in the hub's home directory, which no other replica can read. gcs is required for postgres.

bucket.description: GCS bucket name, no gs:// prefix. Required when database.driver is postgres.

mode.description: Selects which configuration subtree is rendered and nothing else. Every key the HA preflight requires renders identically in both modes.

acknowledgeOAuthUnlanded.description: The oauth mode's client credentials are not rendered by the chart yet. An oauth install starts and passes its probes; every human login fails. Set true to render it anyway.

requireStableSigningKey.description: When true the hub refuses to start rather than fall back to a per-process signing key. That fallback is fatal across replicas and silent: each pod signs tokens the others reject, which presents as intermittent logouts.

allOf.description: postgres requires the Cloud SQL proxy. The derived DSN points at 127.0.0.1, because that is where the proxy listens; with cloudsql.enabled false there is nothing on that port and the hub dials a closed loopback socket, which surfaces as a connection refused that names no cause. Connecting to a Postgres somewhere other than through the proxy is deliberately NOT offered rather than offered untested - this chart has never been run against one, and a database.host value nobody has exercised is a claim the chart cannot support. Adding it later is additive and breaks no existing install; shipping it wrong is not removable.

postgres implies the HA preflight, which requires a GCS bucket. Without this the install succeeds and the hub then refuses to start, so the failure is moved forward to helm template. Skipped when the settings file is supplied wholesale, since the chart is not rendering storage in that case.

oauth mode has no supporting configuration in the chart yet. Requiring an explicit acknowledgement keeps it from being selected by accident. Not applied under config.existingSecret: the chart renders no auth mode there, so auth.mode selects nothing and there is nothing to acknowledge. The same rule is enforced again in the template, on the rendered document, because --skip-schema-validation removes this one.

acknowledgeOAuthUnlanded.description: auth.mode oauth requires auth.acknowledgeOAuthUnlanded true: the client credentials that mode needs are not rendered by this chart yet, and nothing catches that at runtime - the hub starts, passes its probes, and refuses every login.
